chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slaughtered meat of the Jew, and he said, 'It is permissible.' I said, 'Even if he named Al-Masih (the Messiah)?' He said, 'Even if he named Al-Masih, for indeed he only intends Allah.'
ai.seo_question: Is Jewish slaughtered meat halal if they invoke a name other than Allah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the meat of Jews is halal even if they invoke 'Al-Masih' (the Messiah) during slaughter, as their primary intent is directed toward God. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the specific name invoked does not invalidate the slaughter provided the intent remains monotheistic, distinguishing it from polytheistic invocations. It reflects the broader Shia view on the People of the Book, emphasizing the validity of their ritual slaughter despite minor theological differences in their invocation.
